newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Russian Gazprom in deal to supply, transit Armenia.
newsitem.headline: Russian Gazprom in deal to supply, transit Armenia.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly Gazprom and Armenia have agreed to form a joint venture to oversee supplies of Russian gas to and through the former Soviet republic, an Armenian energy official said on Wednesday.

Roland Adonts, chief executive of Armenian state gas concern Armgazprom, said the venture would import Russian natural gas to Armenia for domestic use as well as send some supplies through Armenia to other countries, including to Turkey.
The two countries sealed the deal in principal last January but they took several months to decide how it would function.

Armenia, which produces no gas of its own, suffered critical shortages of energy during the early 1990s following the breakup of the Soviet Union and cutoffs in cheap gas supplies from Turkmenistan and electricity flows. It has debts for the previous gas supplies.
Interfax news agency quoted Armenian energy ministry officials as saying Russian gas supplies to and through Armenia would rise to nine billion cubic metres a year by 2003 from three billion in 1999.
